estimates.outcome: Expert-rated creativity of the participant's ideas (overall novelty and usefulness), both task complexities pooled
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two trained independent external experts, blind to participant demographics, hypotheses and experimental design, rated each idea on overall novelty and usefulness using a five-point scale from extremely low to extremely high. Their average was used as the overall creativity score for each participant's ideas (PDF p. 5, Measurements).
estimates.treatment_arm: LLM partner (simple and complex tasks pooled)
estimates.control_arm: Human partner (simple and complex tasks pooled)

stats.difference_is: No raw difference is printed. The printed t and d are oriented human partner minus LLM partner, opposite to the treatment/control ordering here; their signs are retained.

sources.locator: PDF p. 5, Results, Experiment 1, Self-reported creativity, paragraph beginning "To explore the reasons behind this gap" (objective expert-rated creativity)
PDF p. 6, Fig. 2 caption, analyzed sample for Experiment 1

estimates.notes: The result is the expert-rated output outcome even though its paragraph is under the Self-reported creativity heading. The displayed arm order in the paper is human then LLM. No effect sign has been reversed and no mean difference has been computed. The printed confidence interval is retained in the generic CI fields with ci_of=null because the paper does not name its estimand; it does not contain the printed d and is not assigned to paper_effect. The standardizer used for d is unspecified. The paper also reports a one-way ANOVA and a factorial partner-type main effect for the same pooled outcome on the same page; these are alternate analyses of this contrast, not additional samples or arm comparisons. The t test and accompanying arm descriptives are retained as this contrast's statistics. Arm counts and explicit standard errors are not printed. Task-specific simple effects are excluded as conditional/moderation results under extraction rule 5.

estimates.outcome: Expert-rated creativity of the participant's ideas (overall novelty and usefulness), pooled LLM response-type main effect
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two well-trained experts independently coded creativity using the same overall-novelty-and-usefulness scale as in Experiment 1, a five-point scale from extremely low to extremely high. Their average was used as the overall creativity score of each participant's ideas (PDF p. 5, Measurements for both experiments).

stats.difference_is: No pooled signed difference or regression coefficient is printed.

paper_effect.standardizer: Reported as partial eta squared, not ordinary eta squared; denominator not defined in the paper.

sources.locator: PDF p. 6, Results, Experiment 2, Creativity, LLM response-type main effect in the factorial ANOVA
PDF p. 7, Fig. 4 caption, analyzed sample for Experiment 2

estimates.notes: Full-sample response-type main effect from the factorial ANOVA crossing response type with task complexity. The proposed constrained-responsive configuration is treatment and batch-responsive is control. The schema's eta2 type contains the paper's partial eta squared. F and partial eta squared are unsigned; the paper supplies no pooled means or signed coefficient, so no direction is inferred and no signed standardized effect is computed. No pooled SDs, arm counts, explicit standard errors, or confidence interval are printed. Means and dispersions appear only for the task-specific simple effects; they are not averaged or substituted into this pooled record. Those conditional/moderation results are excluded under extraction rule 5.

open_items: Randomized and analyzed counts for individual cells and for pooled AI/comparison arms are not printed in the saved article. Supplementary demographic Tables S5-S6 may clarify them. Counts are not inferred from degrees of freedom, percentages, balanced-design assumptions, or deposited participant rows.

The estimand of the confidence interval accompanying the pooled expert-creativity comparison in S1 is not identified. Its bounds do not contain the printed d. ci_of remains null, and the bounds are not used as an interval for d. The standardizer for the printed d is also unspecified (PDF p. 5).

S2 has no printed pooled arm means, pooled participant SDs, arm counts, signed treatment contrast, or explicit uncertainty for a signed effect; the factorial F statistic and partial eta squared do not establish its direction (PDF p. 6).

The external supplement remains unchecked. The saved PDF contains no appendix or embedded supplement. The article refers to procedural details, demographic tables and mediation regressions in external supplementary material (PDF pp. 3-7 and 10). Direct urllib requests to the publisher article and the named OSF project API both failed with WinError 10013 socket-access restrictions in this job. No supplementary results are assumed absent.

Overlap between participants in S1 and S2 is unknown. The paper does not say that recruitment was separate or that prior participants were excluded. No combined unique-person total is inferred. The screening sample_overlap field names no other paper sharing this sample (PDF pp. 4-5).

ERNIE Bot version and release year are not stated; ai_tool.year is null. Participant country and recruitment channel are not stated. The Chinese-language context described in the Discussion does not confirm the country of recruitment (PDF pp. 3-5 and 8).

The excluded conditional creativity analyses have unresolved dispersion labels and possible decimal errors; figure captions label the error bars as standard errors while the text labels the cell dispersions as SDs. S1 also has an inconsistent complex-task test. These numbers have not been corrected or substituted into pooled outcomes (PDF pp. 5-7).

The excluded S2 fixation moderated-mediation index has a sign/description conflict and repeats the S1 index. The reference ideas used to score fixation in the human-partner arms and the availability of participant-to-LLM chat are also unclear; the external supplement or authors may clarify these points (PDF pp. 3-7).
notes: The complete markdown conversion was read in order through the references and end matter, and all ten PDF pages were checked with PyMuPDF text extraction. Statistical passages used in estimates were additionally viewed as in-memory PDF crops to verify mathematical signs and punctuation; no image files were created. Mathematical subscripts/superscripts in quotes are linearized, and line breaks are collapsed. Extraction is restricted to full-sample pooled contrasts; task-specific simple effects and moderated-mediation paths are listed as excluded under rule 5. Each experiment reports its recruited sample and states random assignment; those recruitment counts are recorded as n_randomized, with analyzed totals independently printed in figure captions. No exclusions or attrition are reported. The population code follows the reconciled form: paid online participants with prior LLM experience; a named online panel is not established. No preregistration is stated. No eligible across-participant diversity or later unassisted outcome is reported in the saved article. No statistics were computed from data, figures, degrees of freedom or p-values, and printed signs and precision were retained. Only this extraction JSON was written.
